subject.title: [codex] fix(sessions): report archive cleanup in sessions cleanup

question: Should `sessions cleanup --enforce` be allowed to physically remove stale `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` archive files according to the existing retention rules and report those counts in dry-run/apply output?
rationale: The implementation appears correct, but accepting the merge means accepting an operator-visible cleanup behavior that removes retained session archive files and intersects broader archive-retention policy.

options.title: Accept archive-retention cleanup
options.body: Land the PR as-is if maintainers accept removing stale deleted/reset archives under the existing retention rules and the provided CLI proof.

options.title: Ask for broader upgrade proof
options.body: Pause for a large real-store or upgrade-style cleanup transcript if maintainers want more confidence before changing retained artifact behavior.

options.title: Defer to artifact policy work
options.body: Hold or close this PR if maintainers want the broader no-delete/archive naming policy settled before changing cleanup behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept archive-retention cleanup
recommendation.body: Land the PR as-is if maintainers accept removing stale deleted/reset archives under the existing retention rules and the provided CLI proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the sessions cleanup UX and maintenance controls that this PR changes at the command/operator boundary.
